fluff.overview:
The Hercules is a 7,200-ton Spheroid troop transport designed to carry a combined-arms force of armor and infantry into contested landing zones. Introduced in 3053, the vessel was developed as a dedicated armored vehicle carrier to fill a gap in military transport capacity that existing designs could not adequately address. Built using many components shared with an established DropShip class, the Hercules benefited from accelerated development timelines and a ready supply of spare parts from its first day of service.

The design rapidly established a reputation for reliability and versatility, proving itself in combat operations shortly after the prototype's completion. Roughly two vessels per year were produced during its initial manufacturing run, ensuring a steady if modest expansion of the available fleet.
fluff.capabilities:
The Hercules concentrates its heaviest firepower in the nose arc, which mounts a Gauss rifle, an ER PPC, two ER large lasers, four medium lasers, an LRM-20 with Artemis IV fire control, and an AC/5. Each side carries an ER PPC, a large pulse laser, an LRM-15 with Artemis IV, an SRM-6 with Artemis IV, and three medium lasers. The aft arc provides rear defense with an AC/5, an ER large laser, two medium lasers, and an LRM-15 with Artemis IV. One hundred and one double heat sinks manage the thermal load from this diverse weapons suite.

Two immense vehicle holds occupy the lower decks, providing transport and repair facilities for thirty-six heavy vehicles organized as a complete armor battalion. Deck two accommodates twelve heavy vehicles and deck three houses twenty-four, each accessed through massive folding ramp doors. The upper ramps support any vehicle weight, while deck three's ramps are limited to seventy-five tons. Three infantry companies ride on decks five through seven, with vehicle crew quarters on deck four. The bridge on deck nine includes three loading supervisor stations to assist embarking operations with inexperienced troops. At only thirty tons, the armor is light for a vessel of this size, distributed evenly across the hull.
fluff.deployment: The Hercules entered service primarily with the Lyran Alliance Armed Forces, where it became a common sight in combined-arms formations operating against Clan occupation zones. The design's ability to deliver a full armor battalion with infantry support in a single landing made it particularly valuable for planetary assault operations where rapid force projection was essential. Service continued across multiple successor states into the thirty-second century.
fluff.history:
The Hercules was designed and produced by Bowie Industries of Alarion in the Lyran half of the Federated Commonwealth. The vessel shares many components with the venerable Overlord class, a deliberate design decision that contributed greatly to rapid production rates and a deep pool of available spare parts. Seven vessels had been completed by the time the design was formally evaluated, with five seeing active service against the Clans and four more in production.

The prototype Hercules was deployed with the Thirteenth Donegal Guards during their attack on the Jade Falcon world of La Grave in 3054. The vessel provided armor and infantry support for landings at a contested site, and when a pair of Clan OmniFighters attacked the landing zone intending to destroy the grounded transports, the Hercules's considerable firepower destroyed both fighters. This action was among the first reported attacks on a Clan-held world following the Truce of Tukayyid.

Production continued at roughly two vessels per year before the sundering of the Federated Commonwealth disrupted supply lines. Despite this political upheaval, the Hercules remained in widespread service across the former Federated Commonwealth states and the Free Worlds League well into the thirty-second century, proof of the design's fundamental soundness and the ready availability of Overlord-compatible replacement parts.
